Run an Ensemble of Histories

Source: R/immunity_history.R
run_immunity_ensemble.Rd

Runs [run_immunity_history()] for every combination of the basic reproduction numbers, coverage accuracies and seeds given, so that the uncertainty in present-day immunity can be carried into projections. Each combination is one "world".

Usage

run_immunity_ensemble(
  iso,
  disease,
  R0,
  coverage_accuracy = 1,
  seeds = 1,
  R0_weights = NULL,
  accuracy_weights = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

iso, disease

Country and disease.

R0

Vector of basic reproduction numbers.

coverage_accuracy

Vector of coverage accuracies (multipliers on the odds of vaccination).

seeds

Vector of seeds.

R0_weights, accuracy_weights

Optional weights for the values of `R0` and `coverage_accuracy` (in the same order). Equal weights by default. The weight of a world is the product of the two, shared equally among seeds.

cores

Number of worlds to run in parallel (uses `parallel::mclapply()`; not available on Windows).

...

Further arguments passed to [run_immunity_history()], for example `transmission_history` or `year_end`.

Value

A list of class `prevail_immunity_ensemble` with `worlds` (a list of `prevail_immunity_history` objects, each with a `weight`), `grid` (a data frame of `R0`, `coverage_accuracy`, `seed`, `weight` and each world's summary) and `diagnostics` (weighted summaries across worlds; see [write_immunity_json()] for what they hold).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ens <- run_immunity_ensemble("GBR", "measles", R0 = c(12, 15, 18), coverage_accuracy = c(0.5, 1, 2),
                             seeds = 1:2, year_end = 2025)
write_immunity_json(ens, "GBR_measles.json")
} # }
